conflicts.fact: Ferry's actual landing point / southward drift distance (and the model of the journey)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 puts the landing point B at (6, -2.4) on a 6-square grid, which scales to (60, -24) km. Lesson 4 places it at L(60, -16), 16 km south of Mbita after 2 hours. Lesson 6 says 3 hours, with the ferry travelling ~64.6 km. Lesson 8 uses 3 hours and a resultant after 3 hours of (60, -24). The original phenomenon gives 60 km at 20 km/h, which is 3 hours and 24 km drift. 16 km is inconsistent with a 60 km trip.

conflicts.fact: Duration of travel / engine vector used
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 says 2 hours and uses engine vector e=(60,0) and current c=(0,-16). Lessons 1, 3, 6 and 8 use velocity vectors (20,0) and (0,-8) km/h with 3 hours to cover 60 km.

conflicts.fact: True distance travelled by the ferry
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says ≈64.6 km (21.54×3). Lesson 8 says ≈64.4 km.

conflicts.fact: Bearing of the resultant / corrective heading
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 gives 21.8° south of east. Lesson 8 gives bearing ≈111.8°, which is wrong because 90+21.8 is correct only if measured from north, and says the corrective heading is 066.4° (23.6° north of east). Correct is arcsin(8/20)=23.6° north of east, bearing 066.4°, so that part is consistent; but a heading of 23.6° north of east means 'angled' relative to east, while 111.8° and 21.8° are inconsistent in sense with it only if mislabelled.

conflicts.fact: Direction/scale of ferry diagram in Lesson 1 model
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 model uses 10 km per square, with Arrow A 4 squares (40 km) for the engine, Mbita 6 squares away and Arrow B 2 squares (20 km) south. Later lessons use 1 cm=2 km/h (L3), 1 cm=5 km/h (L6) and 20 km east / 8 km south ratios. 4 squares is not 60 km and 2 squares is not 24 km.

Lesson 1 says the matatu displacement from Nairobi to Nakuru is due north-west. Lesson 4 locates a farmer in Nakuru, which is a separate matter; no direct conflict. Lesson 3 vs 7: Lesson 7's Mbita at (8,4) with Kendu Bay at (4,2) differs from the earlier Mbita (60,0) due east of Kisumu.
